meta.title: iMessage Video Size Limit: About 100 MB — and Why It Drops to 3.5 MB Over MMS (2026) | {{SITE_NAME}}
meta.description: Apple publishes no official number, but iMessage handles videos up to about 100 MB between Apple devices. If the recipient isn't on iMessage, the message falls back to MMS at roughly 1–3.5 MB. See what fits and compress yours in your browser.
og.title: iMessage video size limit: ~100 MB (and 3.5 MB over MMS)
og.description: The unofficial ceiling, the MMS trap when the bubble turns green, and how to compress a video to fit either.
hero.title: iMessage video size limit
hero.lead: Apple doesn't publish a limit, but in practice iMessage delivers videos up to about 100 MB between Apple devices — a couple of minutes of phone footage at full quality. The catch is the green bubble: when the recipient isn't on iMessage, the message goes out as MMS through your carrier, and MMS caps video at roughly 1 to 3.5 MB, which is why a video that sends fine to one friend gets crushed or refused for another.
qa.h2: iMessage video limits at a glance
qa.r3.v: No time limit of its own — only the size counts. Messages does offer to send a long video at lower quality, which is its own compression, not a length cut.
qa.after: Because the limit is unofficial, the exact figure varies a little with iOS version and connection, and Messages may quietly downscale a very large video rather than refuse it. Staying under 100 MB avoids surprises; staying under 3.5 MB is what it takes when the bubble is green.
tool.h2: Get your video under the iMessage limit
tool.lead: Drop the video below. It is compressed to just under 100 MB on your own device — nothing is uploaded — at the best quality that size allows, so it sends first time and looks the way you shot it. For a green-bubble recipient, use the full compressor with a custom target of 3 MB instead.
fit.h2: How much video fits in 100 MB?
fit.lead: Plenty — 100 MB is roomy compared with email or Discord. These rows are what this compressor actually produces from a typical phone recording — full HD, 30 frames a second, with sound.
fit.caption: What 100 MB gives you at different video lengths
fit.r1.q: Full HD at the original quality — nothing is lost
fit.r2.q: Nearly full HD, still sharp on any screen
fit.r3.q: Reduced size — clear on a phone, a little soft on a TV
fit.r4.q: Small picture; watchable, blocky on a big screen
fit.after: Even an hour of footage fits in 100 MB at a small picture size, so length is rarely the problem on iMessage. Over MMS it is the whole problem: at 3.5 MB, about 30 seconds stays watchable and anything past a few minutes has to be cut, which the compressor offers to do for you when a clip is too long.
over.p1: Whether a video arrives intact depends less on its size than on how it travels. Between Apple devices signed into iMessage, it goes over the internet with the ~100 MB ceiling. To an Android phone, or to an iPhone with iMessage off, Messages falls back to MMS through your mobile carrier — and carriers cap MMS at 1 to 3.5 MB, so the video is either shrunk to a blur or fails to send. Since iOS 18, iPhones can also use RCS with Android phones where the carrier supports it, which lifts the ceiling to around 100 MB again, but not every carrier does.
over.p2: For a green-bubble recipient the reliable route is a link — AirDrop for someone nearby, or a shared iCloud, Google Drive or Dropbox link — or a video small enough to survive MMS. Everything on this page runs locally in your browser: your video never leaves your device, and there is no account or watermark.
faq.q1: What is the maximum video size for iMessage?
faq.a1: Apple doesn't publish one. In practice, videos up to about 100 MB deliver reliably between Apple devices on iMessage. Very large videos may be downscaled by Messages rather than refused.
faq.q2: Why does my video send to some people but not others?
faq.a2: Those people are not on iMessage — the bubble is green. The message goes out as MMS through your carrier, which caps video at roughly 1 to 3.5 MB depending on the carrier. The same video sends fine to iMessage users because it never touches MMS.
faq.q3: How do I send a long video from an iPhone to an Android phone?
faq.a3: Use a link: share it from iCloud Photos, Google Drive or Dropbox, or send it through WhatsApp as a document. If RCS is enabled for your carrier, videos up to about 100 MB can go directly. Otherwise, compress to under 3 MB with the full compressor for a short clip.
faq.a4: Sometimes. Messages may offer to send a large video at reduced quality, and the Low Quality Image Mode setting affects photos. Compressing the video yourself first — to just under 100 MB, or smaller — means you choose the trade-off instead of the app.
faq.q5: Is my video uploaded when I compress it here?
faq.a5: No. Compression runs in your browser on your own device — there is no server, no account and no watermark. The only place your video goes is the message you send.
